RPE is "rate of perceived exertion", a 1 to 10 score for how hard a set was. A 10 means you couldn't have done another rep, 9 means one rep left in the tank, 8 means two left, and so on.

It's useful because it adjusts to your day. The same weight can be an 8 when you're fresh and a 10 when you slept badly, so you can push when it feels light and back off when it doesn't. Most working sets land around 7 to 9, and the real grinders are best saved for the last set or two.

If you want, I can help you work out how to use it on a specific lift.
